\expandafter\def\csname exptwo@sentence-ordering\endcsname{Median latency at ONE/QUORUM/ALL was write 1.47/1.86/1.98~ms; read 1.98/2.44/2.48~ms; mixed 1.69/2.14/2.19~ms. \expandafter\def\csname exptwo@sentence-tail\endcsname{The tail widens more than the median: write p99 was 2.20~ms at ONE and 2.90~ms at ALL (1.3$\times$), because ALL waits for the slowest of the three replicas while ONE only needs the fastest.}
\expandafter\def\csname exptwo@sentence-errors\endcsname{All 324,000 operations of the fixed-rate grid succeeded.}
\expandafter\def\csname exptwo@sentence-rate\endcsname{Every fixed-rate cell sustained its target rate, so latency differences are not caused by back-pressure.}
\expandafter\def\csname exptwo@sentence-saturation\endcsname{Closed-loop saturation throughput was 1,523, 1,425 and 1,361 ops/s at ONE, QUORUM and ALL (11\% lower at ALL than at ONE). With RF = N = 3 every replica applies every write whatever the CL, so for writes only the client's waiting time differs; a read at QUORUM or ALL additionally sends one or two digest requests, which adds server work. Because the Python client itself is CPU-bound near saturation, these values are a lower bound on cluster capacity.}
\expandafter\def\csname exptwo@sentence-staleness\endcsname{Pairs with $R+W\le N$ returned 0 stale value(s) in 12,000 probes (0.00\%); pairs with $R+W>N$ returned 0 in 18,000 probes, consistent with the quorum-overlap guarantee. No staleness was observed even without overlap: on a healthy single-host cluster the replica mutations arrive long before the client's next request, so the inconsistency window is shorter than one client round trip. Staleness becomes visible once a replica misses writes (Exp 4b, Exp 5).}
